content.text:
I've built the course registration app in `/work`, and `index.html` is the start page. I loaded all four pages in jsdom (a simulated browser) and ran the main flows with no JavaScript errors. I didn't test in a real browser, so the visual layout and screen-reader behaviour haven't been checked by eye or with assistive technology.

**What each page does**
- **Home (`index.html`):** a colourful banner with a course search box that opens the catalog with your search, stats about the courses, the three registration steps, links for each department, and four featured course cards.
- **Catalog (`catalog.html`):** search as you type, dropdowns to filter by department, level and credits, a sort option, an "only open seats" checkbox and a reset button. Results show as course cards colour-coded by department, with a count of matching courses and a message when nothing matches. Filters are saved in the page address, so links can open with filters already applied.
- **Register (`register.html`):** a form with student details, term and course checkboxes. A side panel adds up your credits against the 18-credit limit. On submit it checks every field, and also blocks going over the limit and choosing two courses that meet at the same time. If everything is valid, a confirmation window lists the courses before anything is saved, and a success message appears afterwards.
- **Profile (`profile.html`):** the student's details, term totals, and a table of registered courses with a total-credits row. Each course has a Drop button that asks for confirmation first, and the page shows a message when no courses are left.

**Shared parts:** the same navigation bar on every page, with the current page marked and a count of registered courses. On small screens it collapses into a Menu button. Registrations and profile details are saved in the browser, so they carry over between pages. The sample data is 17 courses in 8 departments in `data.js`, and the sample student starts with two courses registered.

**Accessibility:**
- A "skip to main content" link, proper page regions and a logical heading order on every page.
- Every form field has a visible label, with hints where useful. Errors appear next to each field and in a list at the top that gets focus, and each item links to its field. The page title also changes when there are errors.
- Results counts, credit totals and drop confirmations are read out to screen readers.
- The confirmation window keeps keyboard focus inside it, closes with Escape, and returns focus to where you were. For dropping a course, focus starts on "Keep course" so the safe choice is the default.
- The table has a caption and labelled columns and rows, and can be scrolled sideways with the keyboard on small screens.
- Clear focus outlines, colour contrast meeting the WCAG AA standard, a 44px minimum size for buttons and links, and support for reduced motion and Windows high-contrast mode. Day names like "Mon" are read out in full.

The page HTML was generated from a small helper script kept outside the project (`/tmp/gen/build.py`), so edit the HTML files directly from now on. I haven't committed anything to git.
